name: Button
summary: A button that runs one action on the screen it sits on, such as "Show departures", in ink (`neutral`) or, for the one main action of a screen, in the brand yellow (`brand`).
whenToUse: Use Button for an action that runs on the screen it sits on and is named in words, such as "Show departures", or, given `selected`, for a toggle whose words are an action, such as "Follow".

alternatives.name: LinkButton
alternatives.when: The action takes the reader to another page or place, such as "Back to the map"

alternatives.name: Link
alternatives.when: The words that go to another page or place sit in a sentence, or stand as plain text

alternatives.name: IconButton
alternatives.when: The action shows as an icon alone, with no words

alternatives.name: Toolbar
alternatives.when: Several actions sit together in one bar, one tab stop moved through with the arrows

alternatives.name: Menu
alternatives.when: More actions than the screen has room for open from one button

alternatives.name: FilterChip
alternatives.when: The thing turned on and off is a filter, in a row of filters

alternatives.name: Switch
alternatives.when: The thing turned on and off is a setting, which takes effect at once

alternatives.name: SegmentedControl
alternatives.when: The choice is one of two to five ways to show one view

props.name: variant
props.description: How much the button stands out: `solid` is filled, for the action a panel is for; `outline` is an edge only, for the actions beside it.

props.name: color
props.description: The intent: `neutral` is ink, for every action but the main one; `brand` is the brand yellow, for the one main action of a screen.

props.name: size
props.description: The button's height: `medium` is `size.button`, `small` is `size.button-sm`, for dense rows and panels.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the button ignores the pointer and the keys. A disabled button leaves the tab order unless `focusableWhenDisabled` is set.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Whether the button fills the width of its container, such as a bottom sheet's main action. Sets `data-full-width`.

props.name: selected
props.description: Whether the button, a toggle such as "Follow", is on: `true` or `false` sets `aria-pressed` and draws the button on or off, and `true` sets `data-selected`. Left out, the button is no toggle and has no `aria-pressed`. The caller keeps the state and flips it in `onClick`.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: An icon before the label, in reading order, so it moves to the right in right-to-left text. Hidden from screen readers: the label names the button.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: An icon after the label, in reading order. Hidden from screen readers: the label names the button.

props.name: children
props.description: The label: the words that name the action, in sentence case. Required in practice: a button with no words is an IconButton.

props.name: className
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-Button`.

props.name: style
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-Button`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-Button`.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: whether the button stays focusable when disabled.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: set it to `false` when `render` gives an element that isn't a `<button>`.

props.name: render
props.description: Inherited from Base UI: swaps the root element and keeps the behaviour, the class and the data attributes.

rules.do: Give one button per screen `color="brand"`, for its main action; the default `neutral` ink is for everything else, so the yellow keeps meaning the main action
rules.dont: Put two brand buttons on one screen, or use `brand` for emphasis: a second yellow action leaves neither the main one

rules.do: Name the action in sentence case, as a verb and what it acts on: "Show departures", "Show whole line"
rules.dont: Write "OK", "Click here", Title Case or an exclamation mark ([Content design](../content-design.md))

rules.do: Use IconButton for a button with an icon and no words, so it gets its required label
rules.dont: Pass only a `startIcon` and no `children`: the icon is `aria-hidden`, so the button has no name

rules.do: Use `solid` for the action a panel is for and `outline` for the actions beside it
rules.dont: Mark the main action with `outline`, or set every action in a row `solid`

rules.do: Take `variant` from `solid` and `outline`, `color` from `neutral` and `brand`, and `size` from `medium` and `small`
rules.dont: Write MUI's `variant="contained"`, `color="primary"` or `size="large"`: Button has none of them, and `brand` is its main action's colour

rules.do: Set `type="submit"` on a form's submit button; Base UI's default is `type="button"`
rules.dont: Rely on a button submitting its form: without `type="submit"` it doesn't

rules.do: Pass `nativeButton={false}` with `render` when it gives an element that isn't a `<button>`
rules.dont: Render a link with `render={<a href="/map" />}` for navigation: LinkButton is that component, and a button that navigates misleads screen readers

rules.do: Keep a brand button out of rows of line and mode badges
rules.dont: Set a brand button among bus badges, whose fill and ink label it shares, where it reads as one

rules.do: Give a toggle `selected`, `true` or `false`, and flip it in `onClick`; leave it out on every button that isn't one
rules.dont: Set `selected={false}` on a plain button: it makes the button a toggle that is off, and a screen reader says "not pressed"

rules.do: Keep a toggle's label the same off and on, "Follow", and let `aria-pressed` say the state ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules))
rules.dont: Change the label of a toggle that uses `selected`, to "Following" or "Unfollow": with `aria-pressed` the state is heard twice, "Following, pressed", or the opposite way, "Unfollow, pressed"

rules.do: Use FilterChip for a filter that turns on and off, and Switch for a setting
rules.dont: Use a Button toggle in a row of filters, where FilterChip's pill shows they belong together

rules.do: Set `disabled` when the action can't run, with a reason in words nearby, or `focusableWhenDisabled` so the button can carry it
rules.dont: Restyle a disabled button with `opacity`: disabled is `color.text.tertiary`, a colour

name: IconButton
summary: A button that runs one action and shows it as an icon alone, such as zoom in or show help, named for screen readers by its required `label`.
whenToUse: Use IconButton for an action shown as an icon alone, one people know at a glance, such as zoom in, close or search.

alternatives.name: Button
alternatives.when: The action is named in words, or its icon would have to be guessed

alternatives.name: LinkButton
alternatives.when: Pressing it takes the reader to another page or place

alternatives.name: Toolbar
alternatives.when: Several actions sit together in one bar, one tab stop moved through with the arrows

alternatives.name: MapControls
alternatives.when: The buttons are the map's own: zoom, centre, the 3D toggle, the compass and the pause

alternatives.name: FilterChip
alternatives.when: The control turns a filter on and off

props.name: label
props.description: The words that name the action, in sentence case, such as "Zoom in". Required: the icon is hidden from screen readers, so these words are the button's name. Never seen, read by screen readers.

props.name: color
props.description: The intent: `neutral` is quiet ink, for every action but the main one; `brand` is the brand yellow, for the one main action of a screen.

props.name: size
props.description: The icon's step in the `size.control` square: `medium` is `icon.size.400`, for icons drawn on the 16 px grid; `large` is `icon.size.450`, for the top bar's icons drawn on the 18 px grid.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the button ignores the pointer and the keys. A disabled button leaves the tab order unless `focusableWhenDisabled` is set.

props.name: children
props.description: The icon, such as an SVG from `packages/perron/icons/` with the `perron-icon` class. Hidden from screen readers: `label` names the button.

props.name: className
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-IconButton`.

props.name: style
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-IconButton`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-IconButton`.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

rules.do: Give `label` the action in sentence case, as a verb and what it acts on: "Zoom in", "Centre the map"
rules.dont: Name the icon rather than the action ("Plus", "Magnifier"), or write Title Case or an exclamation mark ([Content design](../content-design.md))

rules.do: Use IconButton only where the icon is one people know at a glance, such as zoom, locate, close or search, and use [Button](button.md) with words otherwise
rules.dont: Put an icon whose meaning has to be guessed in an IconButton: the label reaches only screen readers, and the eye gets the icon alone

rules.do: Give `size="large"` to an icon drawn on the 18 px grid (`monitor`, `info`), and keep the default `medium` for the 16 px ones
rules.dont: Set `--perron-icon-size` or a width on the icon yourself, or give a 16 px icon `large`: an icon drawn on one grid blurs when scaled to another

rules.do: Give one action per screen `color="brand"`, for its main action
rules.dont: Use `brand` for emphasis, or set two brand actions on one screen

rules.do: Set icon buttons on a panel, a sheet or the top bar's glass, which mark where they sit
rules.dont: Float a `neutral` icon button straight over the map: its transparent fill disappears on the land and water

rules.do: Put each action of a [Toolbar](toolbar.md) in a `ToolbarButton`, so the arrow keys reach it
rules.dont: Put an IconButton inside a Toolbar: it falls out of the arrow-key order and adds a tab stop

rules.do: Use a toggle component, such as FilterChip, for an icon that turns something on and off
rules.dont: Set `aria-pressed` on an IconButton and restyle it: IconButton keeps no pressed state, and a toggle says its state in words

rules.do: Set `disabled` when the action can't run, with `focusableWhenDisabled` so the button can still be reached and its name heard
rules.dont: Restyle a disabled icon button with `opacity`: disabled is `color.text.tertiary`, a colour

agentNotes: An agent labelled an `info` button "About", the page it opens, rather than the action. Write a verb and what it acts on, such as "Show help" (DD-1).

name: LinkButton
summary: A link that looks like a Button: it takes the reader to another page or place, such as "Back to the map" or "Open in Rejseplanen", where a Button runs an action on the screen it sits on.
whenToUse: Use LinkButton for a link shaped like a button, which takes the reader to another page or place, such as "Back to the map" or "Open in Rejseplanen".

alternatives.name: Button
alternatives.when: Pressing it runs an action on the screen it sits on

alternatives.name: Link
alternatives.when: The link sits in a sentence, or stands as plain text

props.name: href
props.description: Where the link goes: a URL or a path. Give it on every LinkButton, unless `render` gives a router's link that brings its own destination.

props.name: variant
props.description: How much the link stands out: `solid` is filled, for the main place a panel leads to; `outline` is an edge only, for the links and actions beside it.

props.name: size
props.description: The link's height: `medium` is `size.button`, `small` is `size.button-sm`, for dense rows and panels.

props.name: fullWidth
props.description: Whether the link fills the width of its container, such as a bottom sheet's main link. Sets `data-full-width`.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: An icon before the label, in reading order, so it moves to the right in right-to-left text. Hidden from screen readers: the label names the link.

props.name: endIcon
props.description: An icon after the label, in reading order. Hidden from screen readers: the label names the link.

props.name: children
props.description: The label: the words that name where the link goes, in sentence case. Required in practice: a link with no words has no name.

props.name: className
props.description: Reaches the root; `className` is merged after `pn-LinkButton`.

props.name: style
props.description: Reaches the root; `className` is merged after `pn-LinkButton`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root element.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

rules.do: Use LinkButton when pressing it goes somewhere: another page, another place in the app, another site
rules.dont: Use LinkButton to run an action, such as showing a line or closing a panel, with an `onClick` that prevents the link: that is a Button

rules.do: Use Button for an action and LinkButton for navigation, even when they sit side by side and look alike
rules.dont: Render a link through Button's `render={<a href="/map" />}`: Base UI gives it `role="button"`, and a screen reader hears a button that navigates

rules.do: Name where the link goes, in sentence case: "Back to the map", "Open in Rejseplanen"
rules.dont: Write "Click here", "Read more", Title Case or an exclamation mark ([Content design](../content-design.md)): the role already says it is a link

rules.do: Give a router's link through `render`, such as `render={<Link to="/map" />}`, so the app's navigation runs and the look stays
rules.dont: Wrap a LinkButton in a router link, or a router link in a LinkButton: two nested `<a>` elements are invalid and make two tab stops

rules.do: Use a plain `<a>` inside a sentence, where a link is part of the text
rules.dont: Put a LinkButton in running text: its height and padding break the line

rules.do: Keep LinkButton in ink; give the screen's one main action to a `brand` Button
rules.dont: Restyle a LinkButton in the brand yellow: brand is never a link ([Intents](README.md#intents))

rules.do: Leave a link out, or show a disabled Button, when there is nowhere to go yet
rules.dont: Render a LinkButton without `href` or `render`, or fake a disabled one with `opacity`: an `<a>` with no `href` is not a link, and disabled is a colour

rules.do: Use IconButton for a control with an icon and no words
rules.dont: Pass only a `startIcon` and no `children`: the icon is `aria-hidden`, so the link has no name

name: Toolbar
summary: A bar of actions that is one tab stop, moved through with the arrow keys, such as the map's zoom and locate controls or a glass group in the top bar.
whenToUse: Use Toolbar for a bar of actions that is one tab stop, moved through with the arrow keys, such as a glass group of controls in the top bar.

alternatives.name: MapControls
alternatives.when: The bar holds the map's zoom, centre and view buttons

alternatives.name: Button
alternatives.when: One action stands alone, named in words

alternatives.name: IconButton
alternatives.when: One action stands alone, shown as an icon

alternatives.name: Menu
alternatives.when: More actions than the bar has room for open from one button

alternatives.name: SegmentedControl
alternatives.when: The buttons pick one of two to five ways to show one view

props.name: orientation
props.description: Which way the bar runs, and so which arrow keys move through it: Left and Right for `horizontal`, Up and Down for `vertical`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether every button in the toolbar is disabled. The buttons stay focusable unless their `focusableWhenDisabled` is `false`.

props.name: children
props.description: The toolbar's `ToolbarButton`s, `ToolbarGroup`s and `ToolbarSeparator`s, in reading order.

props.name: className
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-Toolbar`.

props.name: style
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-Toolbar`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-Toolbar`.

props.name: loopFocus
props.description: Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: whether the arrow keys wrap from one end of the toolbar to the other.

props.name: render
props.description: Inherited from Base UI: swaps the root element and keeps the behaviour, the class and the data attributes.

rules.do: Name every toolbar with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, such as "Map controls", so a screen reader tells it from the next one
rules.dont: Leave a toolbar unnamed: two on a screen are both announced as "toolbar"

rules.do: Put each action in a `ToolbarButton`, so the arrow keys reach it
rules.dont: Put a Button, an IconButton or a plain `<button>` straight into the toolbar: it falls out of the arrow-key order and adds a tab stop

rules.do: Give an icon-only button an `aria-label` that names the action: "Zoom in"
rules.dont: Leave an icon-only button without one: its icon is `aria-hidden`, so the button has no name

rules.do: Open a menu, popover or dialog through `render`, `<ToolbarButton render={<Menu.Trigger />}>`, and set `disabled` on the `ToolbarButton`, not the trigger
rules.dont: Disable the trigger itself: Base UI says the button then leaves the toolbar's arrow-key order

rules.do: Wrap a button in a [Tooltip](tooltip.md) with `<Tooltip trigger={<ToolbarButton … />}>…</Tooltip>`, the tooltip around the button
rules.dont: Pass the tooltip's trigger to `ToolbarButton`'s `render`, as for popups

rules.do: Give one button per screen `color="brand"`, for its main action
rules.dont: Mark several toolbar buttons `brand`, or use it for emphasis: a second yellow action leaves neither the main one

rules.do: Keep a disabled button focusable, the default, so it can explain itself through a tooltip
rules.dont: Restyle a disabled button with `opacity`: disabled is `color.text.tertiary`, a colour

rules.do: Give a toggle in a toolbar, such as the map's 3D view, `selected`, held by the screen, and keep its name the same while on and off
rules.dont: Swap a toggle's name with its state, or draw its on look in the caller's CSS: `selected` sets `aria-pressed` and the on look together

rules.do: Place the toolbar over the map in a pattern, which sets its position and stacking
rules.dont: Set a `z-index` or a margin from the screen edge on the toolbar itself: the component sizes to its content

name: Brand
summary: The Mylder mark beside the wordmark "mylder", drawn in both themes from the tokens, for the brand slot of a top bar or a kiosk bar.
whenToUse: Use Brand wherever the Mylder brand appears in an interface, such as the brand slot of a top bar or a kiosk bar, so the mark follows the theme.

props.name: variant
props.description: `full` sets the mark beside the wordmark, as the brand appears by default; `mark` shows the mark alone, for where space is tight, with the brand name read to screen readers.

props.name: brandNameLabel
props.description: Overrides "Mylder", the brand name seen in the wordmark, shown lowercase, with `variant='full'`, and heard alone with `variant='mark'`.

props.name: className
props.description: Merged after `pn-Brand` on the root

props.name: style
props.description: Reaches the root

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

rules.do: Use Brand wherever the Mylder brand appears in an interface, so the mark follows the theme
rules.dont: Put `mylder-mark.svg` in an `` on a themed ground: a file can't follow the theme, so the ring disappears in dark

rules.do: Keep `variant='full'`, and switch to `variant='mark'` only where space is tight
rules.dont: Show the wordmark alone, or set "mylder" in text beside an icon: the lockup is the mark and the wordmark together

rules.do: Hide the whole Brand, or pick `variant='mark'`, at the screen's own breakpoint, such as `breakpoint.compact-phone`
rules.dont: Hide parts of it with `className`, which can leave a mark that no screen reader hears or a wordmark without its mark

rules.do: Render it as a link to the start screen with `render={<a href="/" />}`, so the name and the link are one stop in the tab order
rules.dont: Wrap it in a `<button>` with its own `aria-label`, or give the link a second name: the brand name is already its accessible name

rules.do: Keep at least the ring's width of clear space around it, as [Logos](../foundations/logos.md#usage) asks
rules.dont: Resize, recolour or restyle the mark with `className`, which breaks its drawn size and turns its colours, which are data states, into others

name: Count
summary: A small pill holding how many there are, such as the "3" after "Delays" in a filter chip or the "12" after "Lines" on a tab, set in tabular figures on an inset or tinted surface.
whenToUse: Use Count for how many there are, as a small pill after the words that say what it counts, in a filter chip, a tab or a heading.

alternatives.name: Stat
alternatives.when: The number is a key figure, set large to read at a glance

alternatives.name: Text
alternatives.when: The number sits in a row or a sentence, in the `data` role

alternatives.name: LineBadge
alternatives.when: The pill names a line

alternatives.name: Tag
alternatives.when: The pill holds a word or two that marks a property, such as "Night bus"

props.name: color
props.description: The intent: what the count means. `neutral` is a plain tally, such as lines on a tab; the status intents tint the pill for a count of good or bad news, such as `danger` for lines with delays. Always beside words that say what is counted, such as "Delays": colour is never the only sign.

props.name: children
props.description: The count, written as the screen shows it: `3`, `'1 204'`, `'99+'`. Leave it out when no data gives the count, and Count shows "—" and says "Unknown". `0` is a count, and shows.

props.name: unknownLabel
props.description: Overrides "Unknown", heard in place of "—" when there is no count

props.name: className
props.description: Joined after `pn-Count` on the root

props.name: style
props.description: Reaches the root

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root element

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

rules.do: Put a Count after the words that say what it counts, with a space between them in the markup: `Delays <Count>3</Count>`
rules.dont: Leave the space out: the accessible name may run the words together, "Delays3"

rules.do: Leave out `children` when no data gives the count, so Count shows "—" and says "Unknown"
rules.dont: Pass `0` or a guess when the count is unknown: the brand never claims more than the data knows

rules.do: Render no Count when there is nothing to count and the screen hides empty tallies
rules.dont: Rely on Count to hide itself at `0`, as MUI's Badge does: `0` is a count, and Count shows it

rules.do: Write the count in the screen's locale, and cap it yourself if the space is short: `'1 204'`, `'99+'`
rules.dont: Squeeze a long count into a narrow chip and let it overflow: Count never wraps or truncates

rules.do: Use a status `color` for a count of good or bad news beside the words that name it, such as `danger` after "Delays"
rules.dont: Let the tint be the only sign, or colour a plain tally such as the number of lines on a tab

rules.do: Use Stat for a key figure and Text with a `data` role for a number in a row or a sentence
rules.dont: Use Count as a key figure or inside running text as a number: it is a small pill for tallies in chips, tabs and headings

rules.do: Use LineBadge to name a line
rules.dont: Put a line's name in a Count: it takes the operator's colour, not an intent

rules.do: Announce a changed count in the screen's own polite live region, when it changes state
rules.dont: Make a Count a live region: a tally that updates every few seconds floods the screen reader

name: FactList
summary: A short list of facts about one thing, each a name and what it is, such as "Operator: Movia" and "Last report: 08:14" about a vehicle, set as a description list in a detail panel or a report.
whenToUse: Use FactList for several facts about one thing, each a name and what it is, such as a vehicle's operator and last report in its detail panel.

alternatives.name: Stat
alternatives.when: The fact is one key figure, set large to read at a glance

alternatives.name: VehicleTable
alternatives.when: People compare the same facts across many vehicles, one row each

alternatives.name: EmptyState
alternatives.when: There are no facts to show

props.name: items
props.description: The facts, in reading order, each `{ label, value, key }`: `label` names the fact, `value` says what it is, and `key` is its React key when the facts change order. Required

props.name: unknownLabel
props.description: Overrides "Unknown", heard in place of "—" for a fact with no value

props.name: className
props.description: Joined after `pn-FactList` on the root

props.name: style
props.description: Reaches the root

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root element

props.name: slotProps
props.type: { item?: ComponentProps<"div", {}, HTMLProps> | undefined; label?: ComponentProps<"dt", {}, HTMLProps> | undefined; value?: ComponentProps<"dd", {}, HTMLProps> | undefined; }
props.description: Props for each part: `item`, `label`, `value`.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: slotProps.item
props.description: Props for every `item` part

props.name: slotProps.label
props.description: Props for every `label` part

props.name: slotProps.value
props.description: Props for every `value` part

rules.do: Leave out an item's `value` when no data gives it, so FactList shows "—" and says "Unknown"
rules.dont: Write "0", "n/a" or a guess for a value nobody knows: the brand never claims more than the data knows

rules.do: Name each fact in a word or two, "Operator", "Last report", and write its value as content design does, "32 km/h"
rules.dont: Put the name inside the value, such as "Speed 32 km/h": the name and value then read as one term with no definition

rules.do: Use FactList for several facts about one thing, such as a vehicle in its detail panel
rules.dont: Use it for one key figure, which is a Stat, or for rows people compare across many things, which is a table

rules.do: Name the list with `aria-labelledby` pointing at the panel's heading when the panel holds more than one list
rules.dont: Give the list a heading inside `items`: every entry is a fact, a name and its value

rules.do: Say a status in words in the value, or show it with a SeverityLabel or a Delay
rules.dont: Colour a value through `className` to say it is good or bad: colour alone tells no screen reader and no colour-blind person

rules.do: Show EmptyState in place of FactList when there are no facts to show
rules.dont: Render FactList with an empty `items` and nothing beside it: an empty list tells the person nothing

rules.do: Keep `render` on the root to another `dl`, or a component that renders one
rules.dont: Swap the root for a `ul` or `div` through `render`: its `dt` and `dd` would sit outside a `dl`, which HTML and axe both fail

rules.do: Announce a changed fact in the screen's own polite live region, when it changes state
rules.dont: Make FactList a live region: a speed or report time that updates every few seconds floods the screen reader

name: Kbd
summary: Kbd shows one key of the keyboard, such as "Esc", "+" or "↑", inside help text, so a sentence like "Keys: + and − zoom, arrows pan, Esc closes panels." shows each key as a key.
whenToUse: Use Kbd for one key of the keyboard in help text, such as "Esc" in "Esc closes panels", so the reader sees it is a key.

props.name: children
props.description: One key, as the keyboard prints it or the platform names it: "Esc", "Enter", "+", "−", "↑". Required: a key with no name says nothing. A combination is one Kbd per key (CR-5).

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

rules.do: Mark a property of a departure, vehicle or line with one or two words: "Night bus", "Replacement bus".
rules.dont: Put a sentence in a tag: say what is happening beside it, in plain sentences, as content design asks.

rules.do: Write the words in sentence case and let the tag set the capitals.
rules.dont: Type the capitals: a screen reader may spell them out letter by letter.

rules.do: Say a status in the words: `color='danger'` on "Cancelled".
rules.dont: Let red or green be the only sign, which fails 1.4.1 and every rider who can't tell them apart.

rules.do: Use `dashed` for something announced but not yet confirmed by live data, and say so in the words where it matters: "Cancellation expected".
rules.dont: Use `dashed` as a quieter look for a property that holds: the dashed edge says "not confirmed", and the brand never claims more than it knows.

rules.do: Name a kind of disruption with SeverityLabel, a line with LineBadge, and a number with Count.
rules.dont: Spell out "Delays", a line's name or a count in a tag: each has its own component, with its own words, colours and figures.

rules.do: Use FilterChip for a filter people turn on and off.
rules.dont: Make a tag a control through `render`: it is smaller than `size.target-min` and has no hover, pressed or selected state.

rules.do: Let a row that holds a tag beside other content wrap, with `flex-wrap: wrap`, or let its other content give way.
rules.dont: Set a tag in a row that can't wrap: its narrowest width is its longest word, so a long word pushes it past the row's edge.

props.description: The typography role, one per job, as [Typography](../foundations/typography.md#roles) gives them: `data` roles for anything compared down a column, `overline` set in capitals. props.name: color
props.description: The intent: what the colour means. `neutral` is main text; `brand` is emphasis on the hero page, never a link; the status intents say on time, warning, late or info, always beside words that say it too, such as "Late" or "+4 min": colour is never the only sign. All six intents, each with its `color.text.*` token, default `'neutral'` (`color.text.primary`) rather than inheriting: every intent has a text token measured at 4.5:1, and text on an inverse or coloured fill is the fill's own component's text, not a Text.

props.name: emphasis
props.description: How strongly neutral text stands out: `primary` for what people read first, `secondary` for supporting text, `tertiary` for hints and captions next to stronger text. Changes nothing with any other `color`. A prop of Text's own, for `color.text.secondary` and `color.text.tertiary`, which are no intent and so can't be `color` values; its values are the tokens' own names.

props.description: The text: a string, an element such as `<strong>` or `<time>`, or a list of both.

props.description: Merged onto the root.

props.description: Reaches the root element, whichever element `render` makes it.

props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

rules.do: Give a heading role its heading element through `render`, at its level in the page's outline: `render={<h2 />}`.
rules.dont: Set a heading's look on a `<span>`: a screen reader's list of headings never finds it.

rules.do: Say a status in words beside its colour: `color='danger'` on "+4 min late".
rules.dont: Let red or green be the only sign, which fails 1.4.1 and every rider who can't tell them apart.

rules.do: Keep `emphasis='tertiary'` for hints and captions next to stronger text.
rules.dont: Set a sentence people must read in tertiary: it misses 4.5:1 on purpose.

rules.do: Set times, countdowns, counts and delays in a `data` role, so their tabular figures line up down a column.
rules.dont: Set a time in `body`, where each digit has its own width and a column of times wobbles.

rules.do: Write an `overline`'s text in sentence case and let the role set the capitals.
rules.dont: Type the capitals: a screen reader may spell them out letter by letter.

rules.dont: Use brand text for a link, or anything that looks like one.

rules.do: Leave `badge` to line badges, the job its role was made for.
rules.dont: Set other text in `badge`: its line height of 1 crowds a second line against the first.

rules.do: Restyle through `className`, with the tokens.
rules.dont: Reach for a raw size or colour in `style`, which leaves the theme and the scale behind.

rules.dont: Write "Success!" or "Something went wrong": content design has no exclamation marks, and the words should say what happened

rules.do: Keep the app inside one `PerronProvider`, so every toast stacks in one region at the bottom of the screen and is read by one live region
rules.dont: Render Toasts with no provider: each gets a region of its own, and two at once overlap

rules.do: Give a toast an action only for what can't wait, such as "Undo", and let it stay until it is closed
rules.dont: Give an action toast a short `autoHideDuration`: a person still hearing the toast can miss the action, and it may be the only way to undo

rules.do: Put an app-wide context an action needs, such as a router's, around `PerronProvider`: the toast renders in `PerronProvider`'s region, not where it is written
rules.dont: Rely on a context between `PerronProvider` and the Toast in the action: the region renders outside it

rules.do: Show a message that must stay while its cause lasts, such as a signal fault, as an Alert in the panel
rules.dont: Use a toast for something the person needs later: it leaves after five seconds

rules.do: Use an AlertDialog for a failure that must stop the task
rules.dont: Use a toast to interrupt: every toast is polite, and waits for the screen reader to finish

alternatives.name: RadioGroup

props.name: disabled

props.name: value

props.name: uncheckedValue
props.description: The value submitted with the form when the checkbox is unchecked. By default, unchecked checkboxes do not submit any value, matching native checkbox behavior.

props.name: form

rules.do: Use Checkbox for an answer or a setting that is on or off on its own, applied when the form is sent, such as agreeing to a notice
rules.dont: Use it for a filter on the map that takes effect at once: that is a FilterChip's, pressed and seen at once

rules.do: Write the label as what ticking it turns on, in sentence case, the same ticked or not: "Show planned works on the map"
rules.dont: Write it as a question or a negative ("Don't show planned works?"): a tick on a negative reads backwards

rules.do: Put a link about the setting next to the checkbox, outside its `children`
rules.dont: Put a link inside the label: a checkbox's content is flattened into its name, so the link can't be reached or pressed

rules.do: Give `name`, and `value` where the form needs more than `"on"`, so the answer reaches the form; connect a form library through its controller
rules.dont: Read the state back from the DOM or keep a hidden input of your own: Base UI's hidden input already carries it

rules.do: Use `indeterminate` for a box that stands for a set partly on, such as "All lines" over the lines below it, and set it from the set's state, or give it `parent` inside a CheckboxGroup with `allValues`, which sets it for you
rules.dont: Use it as a third answer to one question: "mixed" says some of a set, and Space always turns it to ticked or unticked

rules.do: Show why a box is invalid in words, from its field
rules.dont: Rely on the danger edge alone: colour is never the only sign ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules))

rules.do: Group related checkboxes in a CheckboxGroup, whose legend names the group
rules.dont: Make a list of checkboxes one tab stop, or use them for one choice among several: that is a radio group's or a SegmentedControl's

rules.do: Keep `onChange` for the box's state, and cancel it with `details.cancel()` when the change must not happen
rules.dont: Set `aria-checked` yourself or toggle a class: Base UI keeps the state, the attribute and the input in step

name: CheckboxGroup
summary: A named set of checkboxes that answer one question together, such as which modes the map shows, holding the ticked values as one list, with a line of help and an error message tied to the set, submitted with a form under one name, and, where the set needs one, a parent checkbox that ticks or unticks them all.
whenToUse: Use CheckboxGroup for several answers to one question, applied when the form is sent, such as which modes a report covers, with a parent checkbox where the set needs one.

alternatives.name: Checkbox
alternatives.when: One setting or answer is on or off on its own

alternatives.name: RadioGroup
alternatives.when: The answer is one choice among two to six

alternatives.name: SegmentedControl
alternatives.when: The choice is one of two to five ways to show one view

alternatives.name: FilterChip
alternatives.when: The answers are filters on the map, which take effect at once

alternatives.name: Fieldset
alternatives.when: The group holds different controls, such as the fields of a report form, under one name

props.name: label
props.description: Required. The group's name, in sentence case, a few words or a short question, such as "Show on map": shown above the checkboxes, and the group's accessible name.

props.name: hiddenLabel
props.description: Whether the label is heard but not seen. Use it where a heading right above already names the group for the eye, so the group keeps its name for the ear.

props.name: description
props.description: A line of help under the label about the whole set, such as "The map shows vehicles of the ticked modes only", read after each checkbox's name by a screen reader. Left out, no description is rendered.

props.name: error
props.description: What is wrong with the ticked set and how to put it right, such as "Choose at least one mode". Given, it marks the group invalid and is shown under the checkboxes; left out, the group shows Base UI's own message when its `validate` fails.

props.name: onChange
props.type: (event: Event, value: string[], details: CheckboxGroup.ChangeEventDetails) => void
props.description: Called when a click or Space ticks or unticks a checkbox in the group, or a parent checkbox ticks or unticks the set, with the new list of ticked values as `value`; `details.reason` is `'none'`, and `details.cancel()` keeps the list as it was. `event` is `details.event`. Not called while disabled.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether every checkbox in the group ignores the pointer and the keys. They leave the tab order and take the disabled look, with the label, the description and the error; a fieldset round the group disables it too.

props.name: name
props.description: Identifies the group when a form is submitted: each ticked checkbox submits its `value` under this name, and a disabled one submits nothing.

props.name: children
props.description: Required. The group's checkboxes, in reading order: each a Checkbox with its own `value`, which the group's `value` lists while it is ticked, and, with `allValues`, a parent Checkbox first.

props.name: className
props.description: Reaches the root, the group. Merged after `pn-CheckboxGroup`.

props.name: style
props.description: Reaches the root, the group.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root, the group: the `<div role="group">`, or the element `render` gives.

props.name: slotProps
props.type: { legend?: FieldsetLegendProps | undefined; description?: FieldDescriptionProps | undefined; error?: FieldErrorProps | undefined; }
props.description: Props for each part: `legend`, `description`, `error`.

props.name: value
props.description: Names of the checkboxes in the group that should be ticked. To render an uncontrolled checkbox group, use the `defaultValue` prop instead.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: Names of the checkboxes in the group that should be initially ticked. To render a controlled checkbox group, use the `value` prop instead.

props.name: allValues
props.description: Names of all checkboxes in the group. Use this when creating a parent checkbox.

props.name: invalid
props.description: Whether the field is invalid. Useful when the field state is controlled by an external library.

props.name: validate
props.type: (value: unknown, formValues: Form.Values) => string | string[] | null | void | Promise<string | string[] | null | void>
props.description: A function for custom validation. Return a string or an array of strings with the error message(s) if the value is invalid. Returning nothing, `null`, an empty string, or an empty array means the value is valid. Asynchronous functions are supported, but they do not prevent form submission when using `validationMode="onSubmit"`.

props.name: validationMode
props.description: Determines when the field should be validated. This takes precedence over the `validationMode` prop on `<Form>`. `onSubmit`: triggers validation when the form is submitted, and re-validates on change after submission. `onBlur`: triggers validation when the control loses focus. `onChange`: triggers validation on every change to the control value.

props.name: validationDebounceTime
props.description: How long to wait between `validate` callbacks if `validationMode="onChange"` is used. Specified in milliseconds.

props.name: dirty
props.description: Whether the field's value has been changed from its initial value. Useful when the field state is controlled by an external library.

props.name: touched
props.description: Whether the field has been touched. Useful when the field state is controlled by an external library.

props.name: actionsRef
props.description: A ref to imperative actions. `validate`: Validates the field when called.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: slotProps.legend
props.description: Props for the `legend` part, passed to Fieldset's own `slotProps.legend`. Its `id` is the one the group's `aria-labelledby` points at.

props.name: slotProps.description
props.description: Props for the `description` part.

props.name: slotProps.error
props.description: Props for the `error` part, such as `match`, to show a message of the caller's own for one failing check only.

rules.do: Use CheckboxGroup for several answers to one question that are applied when the form is sent, such as which modes a report covers
rules.dont: Use it for filters on the map that take effect at once: those are FilterChips, pressed and seen at once

rules.do: Give every checkbox a `value` of its own, and read and set the ticked set through the group's `value` and `onChange`
rules.dont: Give the checkboxes `checked`, `defaultChecked` or `onChange` of their own to keep the set: the group's `value` overrides them, and a box with no `value` takes the group's name

rules.do: Write the legend in sentence case as the question the set answers, "Show on map", and each label as an answer, "Bus"
rules.dont: Repeat the legend's words in every label ("Show bus on map"): the screen reader reads the group's name before each box already

rules.do: Give `name` so the ticked values reach the form, and connect a form library through its controller
rules.dont: Keep a hidden input of your own for the list: Base UI's hidden inputs already submit each ticked box

rules.do: Say what is wrong in words, through `error` or a `validate` that returns the message, such as "Choose at least one mode"
rules.dont: Rely on the checkboxes' danger edges alone: colour is never the only sign ([Accessibility](../foundations/accessibility.md#rules))

rules.do: Use `description` for help about the whole set, such as what ticking means
rules.dont: Put help or an error as plain text among the checkboxes: nothing ties it to the group for the ear

rules.do: Disable the whole group with `disabled`, so every box goes together
rules.dont: Disable each box by hand in a group that stays enabled: the legend then looks live over dead boxes

rules.do: Use a radio group or a SegmentedControl for one choice among several
rules.dont: Use a CheckboxGroup for one choice: a set of checkboxes says any number may be ticked, none included

rules.do: Put a parent Checkbox, with `parent` and no `value`, first in the group and name it for the set, "All modes", and list every other checkbox's `value` in `allValues`
rules.dont: Leave a value out of `allValues`, or indent the boxes under the parent with a wrapper of your own: the parent counts only what `allValues` lists, and a wrapper takes the boxes out of the group's column

rules.do: Use a single Checkbox for one on-or-off setting
rules.dont: Wrap one checkbox in a CheckboxGroup: a group of one adds a name the checkbox's own label already gives

rules.do: Group controls that answer one question, such as which modes to show, or fields that belong together, such as a report's place and time
rules.dont: Wrap a single control in a Fieldset: one control is named by its own label, through Field

rules.do: Write the legend in sentence case, a few words or a short question: "Show on the map"
rules.dont: Put a heading element inside `legend`, or type it in capitals: the legend is already the group's name, a heading inside it adds one to the page's outline that no section follows, and capitals come only from the overline style

rules.do: Use CheckboxGroup or RadioGroup for a set of checkboxes or radios, once they ship: they compose Fieldset with the group's behaviour
rules.dont: Render Fieldset as a Base UI group yourself in a screen: the groups hold the value, the keys and the form name for you

rules.do: Disable the whole group with `disabled`, so every control in it goes together
rules.dont: Disable each control by hand inside a Fieldset that stays enabled: the legend then looks live over dead controls

rules.do: Use `hiddenLegend` where a heading right above already names the group for the eye
rules.dont: Leave out the legend, or replace it with an `aria-label` on the root: the legend is the group's one name, seen and heard alike

rules.do: Use Section for a titled block of content in a panel
rules.dont: Use Fieldset to title content that holds no controls: a `group` with nothing to fill in tells a screen reader there is something to fill in

rules.do: Give the group's description and error through a Base UI `Field.Root`, as CheckboxGroup and RadioGroup do
rules.dont: Put a hint or an error as plain text among the controls: nothing ties it to the group for the ear

name: FilterChip
summary: A pill that turns one filter on and off, such as "Delays" in the top bar's filters, with an optional icon before its words and a count after them, drawn in ink when it is on.
whenToUse: Use FilterChip for a filter people turn on and off on its own, in a row of filters, such as showing delays on the map.

alternatives.name: SegmentedControl
alternatives.when: The choice is one of two to five views or modes, and only one holds at a time

alternatives.name: HighlightChip
alternatives.when: One highlight floats over the map, such as a line in focus

alternatives.name: Switch
alternatives.when: The thing turned on and off is a setting, which takes effect at once

alternatives.name: Tag
alternatives.when: A property is marked and can't be pressed

props.name: selected
props.description: Whether the filter is on, when the caller controls it. Announced as pressed.

props.name: defaultSelected
props.description: Whether the filter is on at first, when FilterChip keeps the state itself.

props.name: onChange
props.type: (event: Event, value: boolean, details: Toggle.ChangeEventDetails) => void
props.description: Called when a click, Enter or Space turns the filter on or off, with the new state as `value`; `details.reason` is `'none'`, and `details.cancel()` keeps the state as it was. `event` is `details.event`.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the chip ignores the pointer and the keys. A disabled chip leaves the tab order and keeps its state.

props.name: startIcon
props.description: An icon before the label, in reading order, such as the disruption icon of the kind the chip filters. Hidden from screen readers: the label names the chip.

props.name: count
props.description: How many the filter matches, shown after the label as a [Count](count.md), such as the "3" of "Delays 3". Heard after the label. Shown for `0` too; left out when `undefined` or not a finite number.

props.name: children
props.description: The label: the name of what the filter shows, in sentence case, such as "Delays". It stays the same whether the filter is on or off.

props.name: className
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-FilterChip`.

props.name: style
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-FilterChip`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-FilterChip`.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

props.name: render
props.description: Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

rules.do: Use FilterChip for a filter people turn on and off on its own, such as showing delays on the map
rules.dont: Use it to pick one of several views or modes: that is one choice, a SegmentedControl's, and chips would let two be on at once

rules.do: Keep the label the filter's name, the same on and off, in sentence case: "Delays", "Planned works"
rules.dont: Change the label to say the state ("Delays on"): `aria-pressed` and the fill already say it, and a changing label moves the row

rules.do: Give the count as `count`, so every chip's count has Count's shape and is heard after the label
rules.dont: Build a count into `children`, or pass a guess when the number is unknown: leave `count` out, and the chip shows none

rules.do: Use the [content design](../content-design.md) words for kinds of disruption and data states, so the chips agree with the rest of Mylder
rules.dont: Coin a filter name of your own for a kind the table names

rules.do: Lay a row of chips out with `flex-wrap: wrap` and a gap, and name the group in the pattern that holds it
rules.dont: Put chips in a [Toolbar](toolbar.md) or make them one tab stop: each is a filter of its own, reached with Tab

rules.do: Use a [Tag](tag.md) to mark a property that can't be pressed
rules.dont: Use a FilterChip as a label: a chip invites a press, and one that does nothing misleads

rules.do: Disable a chip only while its filter can't apply, and say why nearby
rules.dont: Disable a chip to show a count of 0: show the 0, since a disabled chip leaves the tab order and can't explain itself

rules.do: Keep `onChange` for the filter's state, and cancel it with `details.cancel()` when the change must not happen
rules.dont: Set `aria-pressed` yourself or toggle a class: Base UI keeps the state and the attribute in step

name: HighlightChip
summary: A pill that floats over the map on glass and turns one highlight of the map on and off, such as line 5C in focus with everything outside it dimmed; while it is selected, the map shows the highlight.
whenToUse: Use HighlightChip for the one highlight that floats over the map, such as line 5C in focus with everything outside it dimmed, which the rider turns on and off.

alternatives.name: FilterChip
alternatives.when: A filter turns on and off in a row of filters, in a panel or the top bar

alternatives.name: SegmentedControl
alternatives.when: The choice is one of two to five ways to show one view

props.name: selected
props.description: Whether the highlight is on, when the caller controls it. Announced as pressed.

props.name: defaultSelected
props.description: Whether the highlight is on at first, when the chip keeps the state itself.

props.name: onChange
props.type: (event: Event, value: boolean, details: Toggle.ChangeEventDetails) => void
props.description: Called when a click, Enter or Space turns the chip on or off, with the next selected state: `true` turns the highlight on, `false` clears it. `event` is `details.event`, and `details.cancel()` keeps the chip as it was.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the chip ignores the pointer and the keys. A disabled chip leaves the tab order, and a selected one still shows that the highlight is on.

props.name: children
props.description: Required. What the chip highlights, in a word or two in sentence case, such as "Line 5C" or "Delayed vehicles": the chip's name. A string, an element such as a LineBadge, or a list of both.

props.name: className
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-HighlightChip`.

props.name: style
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-HighlightChip`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-HighlightChip`.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

rules.do: Name what the chip highlights in a word or two: "Line 5C", "Delayed vehicles".
rules.dont: Write an instruction such as "Click to highlight": `aria-pressed` already says it is a toggle and whether it is on.

rules.do: Float one chip over the map, placed by the screen with `z-index.highlight`, and clear it on Esc after a dialog and a detail panel.
rules.dont: Put a row of highlight chips in a panel or the top bar: a filter people turn on and off there is a FilterChip, and a choice of views a SegmentedControl.

rules.do: Control it with `selected` when the map can change the highlight too, such as a click on another line.
rules.dont: Keep a second copy of the state beside an uncontrolled chip: the two drift apart, and the chip says the highlight is on when it is not.

rules.do: Put a LineBadge or an icon in `children` beside the words when it helps the eye find the line.
rules.dont: Give the chip a badge or an icon alone: its content is its name, and a screen reader needs the words.

rules.do: Keep the words the same, on and off, and let `aria-pressed` say whether the highlight is on.
rules.dont: Restyle the selected chip through `className` to look like the unselected one: the inverse fill is what tells the eye the highlight is on.

rules.do: Let the chip wrap in a narrow container: it grows taller and keeps every word.
rules.dont: Cut its words off with `nowrap` and an ellipsis through `className`: a Danish line name at 320 px would lose its end.

name: NumberField
summary: The box a person types a number into, or steps up and down with its minus and plus buttons and the arrow keys, such as how many departures a board shows, framed by the Field that gives it its label, its line of help and its error message.

props.name: label
props.description: Required. The field's name, in sentence case, such as "Departures to show": shown above the box, and the input's accessible name.

props.name: hiddenLabel
props.description: Whether the label is heard but not seen. Use it only where the screen around the field already says what it is for.

props.name: optional
props.description: Whether the person may leave the field empty. Adds "(optional)" after the label's words, seen and heard as part of the input's name. It sets no check: `required` does.

props.name: optionalLabel
props.description: Overrides "(optional)", the mark after the label's words with `optional`.

props.name: description
props.description: A line of help between the label and the box, such as "From 1 to 20", read after the label by a screen reader. Left out, no description is rendered.

props.name: error
props.description: What is wrong with the number and how to put it right, such as "Enter a number from 1 to 20". Given, it marks the field invalid and is shown under the box; left out, the field shows Base UI's own message when the number fails its checks.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Whether the field ignores the person: the box takes no focus, no typing and no presses, and the label, the help, the number and the buttons turn to the tertiary ink.

props.name: onChange
props.type: (event: Event, value: number | null, details: NumberField.Root.ChangeEventDetails) => void
props.description: Called when the number changes: as the person types a number that parses (`details.reason` `'input-change'`), clears the box (`'input-clear'`, `value` `null`), leaves it and the number is clamped or rounded (`'input-blur'`), pastes (`'input-paste'`), steps it with the keys (`'keyboard'`), presses a button (`'increment-press'`, `'decrement-press'`) or turns the wheel (`'wheel'`), or the browser autofills Base UI's hidden input (`'none'`). `event` is `details.event`, and `details.cancel()` keeps the number as it was.

props.name: onChangeCommitted
props.type: (event: Event, value: number | null, details: NumberField.Root.CommitEventDetails) => void
props.description: Called once the person has settled on a number: when they leave the box after typing, release a held button, or with each key step and wheel turn; `event` is `details.event`. Use it to save or fetch, where `onChange` fires on every step of a held button.

props.name: locale
props.description: The locale the number is written and read in: "1,500" in English, "1.500" in Danish, "1 500" in Swedish and Norwegian. Left out, the nearest PerronProvider's.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Words shown in the empty box, such as "Such as 8". They vanish as the person types, so they never replace the label or the description.

props.name: increaseLabel
props.description: Overrides "Increase", the increment button's name.

props.name: decreaseLabel
props.description: Overrides "Decrease", the decrement button's name.

props.name: numberFieldLabel
props.description: Overrides "Number field", what a screen reader calls the input in place of its role (Owned strings).

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root, the `NumberField.Root` `<div>`.

props.name: slotProps
props.type: { field?: Omit<FieldRootProps, "children" | "disabled" | "name"> | undefined; label?: FieldLabelProps | undefined; description?: FieldDescriptionProps | undefined; error?: FieldErrorProps | undefined; group?: NumberFieldGroupProps | undefined; input?: NumberFieldInputProps | undefined; decrement?: NumberFieldDecrementProps | undefined; increment?: NumberFieldIncrementProps | undefined; }
props.description: Props for each part: `field`, `label`, `description`, `error`, `group`, `input`, `decrement`, `increment`.

props.name: value
props.description: The raw numeric value of the field.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The uncontrolled value of the field when it's initially rendered. To render a controlled number field, use the `value` prop instead.

props.name: name
props.description: Identifies the field when a form is submitted.

props.name: min
props.description: The minimum value of the input element.

props.name: max
props.description: The maximum value of the input element.

props.name: step
props.description: Amount to increment and decrement with the buttons and arrow keys, or to scrub with pointer movement in the scrub area. To always enable step validation on form submission, specify the `min` prop explicitly in conjunction with this prop. Specify `step="any"` to always disable step validation; interactive stepping then uses a base amount of `1`, while the alt and shift keys still step by `smallStep` and `largeStep`.

props.name: smallStep
props.description: The small step value of the input element when incrementing while the alt key is held. Snaps to multiples of this value when `snapOnStep` is enabled.

props.name: largeStep
props.description: The large step value of the input element when incrementing while the shift key is held. Snaps to multiples of this value when `snapOnStep` is enabled.

props.name: snapOnStep
props.description: Whether the value should snap to the nearest step when incrementing or decrementing.

props.name: allowOutOfRange
props.description: When true, direct text entry may be outside the `min`/`max` range without clamping, so native range underflow/overflow validation can occur. Step-based interactions (keyboard arrows, buttons, wheel, scrub) still clamp.

props.name: allowWheelScrub
props.description: Whether to allow the user to scrub the input value with the mouse wheel while focused and hovering over the input.

props.name: format
props.description: Options to format the input value.

props.name: readOnly
props.description: Whether the user should be unable to change the field value.

props.name: required
props.description: Whether the user must enter a value before submitting a form.

props.name: id
props.description: The id of the input element.

props.name: form
props.description: Identifies the form that owns the hidden input. Useful when the number field is rendered outside the form.

props.name: inputRef
props.description: A ref to access the hidden input element.

props.name: render
props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: className
props.description: CSS class applied to the element, or a function that returns a class based on the component's state.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: slotProps.field
props.description: Props for the `field` part, the frame: Base UI's `invalid`, `validate`, `validationMode`, `validationDebounceTime`, `dirty`, `touched` and `actionsRef`, and a `className` or `style` for the frame.

props.name: slotProps.label
props.description: Props for the `label` part.

props.name: slotProps.description
props.description: Props for the `description` part.

props.name: slotProps.error
props.description: Props for the `error` part, such as `match`, to show a message of the caller's own for one failing check only, as `match="rangeOverflow"`.

props.name: slotProps.group
props.description: Props for the `group` part, the box.

props.name: slotProps.input
props.description: Props for the `input` part, such as `autoFocus`, or an `onBlur` of the caller's own.

props.name: slotProps.decrement
props.description: Props for the `decrement` part, the button that steps the number down.

props.name: slotProps.increment
props.description: Props for the `increment` part, the button that steps the number up.

name: RadioGroup

props.name: className

props.name: inputRef
props.description: Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: a ref to access the hidden input element.

props.name: render
props.description: Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component.

props.description: Props for the `legend` part, merged under Perron's own; its `className` joins after `pn-RadioGroup-legend`, and its `id` is the one the group's `aria-labelledby` points at.

name: SearchField
summary: The field that finds a line or a stop: a labelled text input with the search icon, a clear button while it holds text, and a list of suggestions under it that narrows as the person types.

props.name: label
props.description: Required. The field's name, in sentence case, such as "Search lines and stops": shown above the box, and the input's accessible name.

props.name: hiddenLabel
props.description: Whether the label is heard but not seen. Use it where the icon and the placeholder make the field's purpose plain, as in the top bar.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Words shown in the empty box, such as "Line or stop, such as 5C". They vanish as the person types, so they never replace the label.

props.name: items
props.description: Required. The suggestions: each with a `value` that identifies it, the `label` shown and filled into the box when it is chosen, and an optional `description` and `startIcon`.

props.name: filter
props.description: Whether an item matches the typed words. Left out, an item matches when its label contains them, ignoring case and accents. `null` shows `items` as given, for suggestions the caller has already matched, such as from a server.

props.name: value
props.description: The words in the box, when the caller controls them.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The words in the box at first, when SearchField keeps them itself. Left out, the box starts empty.

props.name: onChange
props.type: (event: Event, value: string, details: Autocomplete.Root.ChangeEventDetails) => void
props.description: Called when the words change: by typing (`details.reason` `'input-change'`), by a chosen item filling them (`'item-press'`), by the clear button (`'clear-press'`), or by Esc with the list closed (`'escape-key'`). `event` is `details.event`.

props.name: open
props.description: Whether the list of suggestions is shown, when the caller controls it.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the list is shown at first, when `open` is not set.

props.name: onOpen

props.name: onClose

props.description: Called when the list asks to close: `reason` is `'escape-key'`, `'outside-press'`, `'focus-out'`, `'item-press'`, `'input-clear'`, `'close-press'`, or `'none'` for Enter with no row highlighted; `details.cancel()` keeps it open.

props.name: onItemSelect
props.description: Called when the person chooses a suggestion, with a press or with Enter on the highlighted row, with the item itself.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root, the `Field.Root` `<div>`.

props.name: clearLabel
props.description: Overrides "Clear", the clear button's name.

props.name: noMatchesLabel
props.description: Overrides "No matches", the message the list shows and announces when no suggestion matches.

props.name: render

name: Select
summary: The field that picks one value from a short, fixed list: a labelled box showing the chosen option, or a placeholder, that opens a list of options under it, with the field's help and error round it.

props.name: items
props.description: Required. The options, in order: each with a `value` that identifies it and the `label` shown in its row and in the box once chosen, and `disabled` for one that can't be chosen; or groups, each with a `label` and its own `items`.

props.name: placeholder
props.description: Words shown in the box while no option is chosen, such as "Choose a transport mode". They never replace the label.

props.name: value
props.description: The chosen option's `value`, or `null` for none, when the caller controls it.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The option chosen at first, when Select keeps the value itself. Left out, nothing is chosen.

rules.do: Use a Switch for a setting that takes effect the moment it changes, such as showing vehicle trails or the stations on the map
rules.dont: Use it for an answer a form sends later with a button: a checkbox says "choose now, apply on submit", where a switch says "this is on now"

rules.do: Name it with a visible `<label>` or a Field's label that names the setting, in sentence case: "Show vehicle trails"
rules.dont: Leave it unnamed, or name it with `aria-label` where there is room for a visible label: a sighted person can't tell what an unlabelled switch turns on

rules.do: Keep the label the same whether the switch is on or off
rules.dont: Write the state in the label, "Trails on", or swap it when the switch flips: the switch already says on or off, and a changing label reads as a second state

rules.do: Put the label before the switch in a settings row, and let a long label wrap
rules.dont: Squeeze the switch to fit a long label, or cut the label off: the track keeps its size, and a Danish label is longer than its English

rules.do: Filter the map's vehicles with a [FilterChip](filter-chip.md), and pick one way of showing a view with a [SegmentedControl](segmented-control.md)
rules.dont: Use a row of switches for one choice of several, or for the top bar's filters: switches each turn their own setting on, and a chip shows its count

rules.do: Run an action, such as following a vehicle, with a [Button](button.md)
rules.dont: Use a switch to start something that then runs on its own: a switch holds a state, it doesn't trigger one

rules.do: Say why a switch is disabled or read-only, in its label or the Field's description
rules.dont: Disable a switch with no word of why: a dimmed switch can't explain itself

props.name: render

props.name: style

props.description: Props for the `field` part, the frame: Base UI's `invalid`, `validate`, `validationMode`, `validationDebounceTime`, `dirty`, `touched` and `actionsRef`, and a `className` or `style` for the frame.

props.name: slotProps.description

rules.do: Give a `label` that names the words, "Stop name", and hide it with `hiddenLabel` only where the screen already says it
rules.dont: Let the `placeholder` stand in for the label: it vanishes as the person types, and it is drawn in `color.text.tertiary`, below text contrast

rules.do: Put help the person needs while typing in `description`, "As written on the stop sign"
rules.dont: Put that help in the `placeholder`: it is gone once they type

rules.do: Word an `error` as what to do, "Enter a stop name"
rules.dont: Blame the person or say only that it failed ("Invalid input"), against [Content design](../content-design.md)

rules.do: Spread React Hook Form's `register('stop')` on TextField, or pass Formik's `handleChange`, as on a native `<input>`
rules.dont: Wrap TextField in a controller to read its value: its `onChange` is the native one already

rules.do: Give `error` from the form library whenever the field is invalid
rules.dont: Set `slotProps.field.invalid` with no message: the red edge alone tells only the eye, and only by its colour

rules.do: Give `autoComplete` for the person's own details, such as `autoComplete="email"`, so the browser can fill them
rules.dont: Leave a field that asks for a name, an email address or a phone number without `autoComplete`: WCAG 2.2's identify input purpose (1.3.5) asks for it

rules.do: Set `optional` on the few fields the person may leave empty, and `required` where an empty field must fail
rules.dont: Write "(optional)", "(required)" or an asterisk into `label` yourself: it misses the locale, and an asterisk needs a legend

rules.do: Use SearchField to find a line or a stop, and NumberField for a number
rules.dont: Give TextField a `type` of `'search'` or `'number'`: the type union leaves them out, and SearchField and NumberField carry their own keys and words

rules.do: Use TextField on its own: it already has its label, its help and its error
rules.dont: Wrap TextField in Field: the input would be labelled twice, as Field's spec says

rules.do: Set the width on the container, or on the frame through `slotProps.field`
rules.dont: Give the input a width through `style` alone: the label and the error take the frame's width, not the box's

name: Accordion
summary: A stack of headed sections, each opening and closing its own content under its heading, such as the questions on a help panel or the details of each planned work on a line.
whenToUse: Use Accordion for a stack of headed sections a person reads one or two of, each opening under its heading, such as the questions on a help panel or the details of each planned work on a line.

alternatives.name: Tabs
alternatives.when: The sections are views of one thing, one showing at a time in the same place

alternatives.name: Section
alternatives.when: Most people need the content, such as a stop's next departures, so it stays shown under its heading

props.name: value
props.description: The `value`s of the open items, when the caller controls them. `[]` opens none.

props.name: defaultValue
props.description: The `value`s of the items open at first, when Accordion keeps them itself. Left out, every item starts closed.

props.name: onChange
props.type: (event: Event, value: string[], details: Accordion.Root.ChangeEventDetails) => void
props.description: Called when an item opens or closes, with the `value`s of the items open after it: by a press, Enter or Space on a trigger (`details.reason` `'trigger-press'`), or by the browser's find in page with `hiddenUntilFound` (`'none'`). `event` is `details.event`.

props.name: children
props.description: The `AccordionItem`s, in reading order.

props.name: className
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-Accordion`.

props.name: style
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-Accordion`.

props.name: ref
props.description: Reaches the root. `className` is merged after `pn-Accordion`.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: whether multiple items can be open at the same time.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: whether the component should ignore user interaction. Every trigger is then `disabled`.

props.name: hiddenUntilFound
props.description: Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: allows the browser's built-in page search to find and expand the panel contents, keeping closed panels mounted with `hidden="until-found"`. Overrides `keepMounted`.

props.name: keepMounted
props.description: Inherited from Base UI with its JSDoc: whether to keep each panel in the DOM, `hidden`, while it is closed. Ignored with `hiddenUntilFound`.

props.name: render
props.description: Inherited from Base UI: swaps the root element and keeps the behaviour, the class and the data attributes.

rules.do: Use Accordion for sections a person reads one or two of, such as help questions or the details of each planned work
rules.dont: Hide what most people need behind a heading, such as a stop's next departures: show it, under a [Section](section.md)

rules.do: Use [Tabs](tabs.md) to switch between views of one thing
rules.dont: Use Accordion as tabs stacked down the page: an accordion's sections are read in place, one under another

rules.do: Write each `title` as a few words or a short question in sentence case, saying what the panel holds: "What the dot shapes mean"
rules.dont: Write "Read more" or "Details" on every item: each trigger and its region are named by the title, so every one would sound the same

rules.do: Keep a title to words: an icon or a badge beside it is fine, a link or a button is not
rules.dont: Put a link or a button in a `title`: it renders inside the trigger's `<button>`, where nothing else can be pressed

rules.do: Give items a `value` when the accordion opens one at first or the caller controls it
rules.dont: Read a generated value from `onChange` and store it: it changes from one mount to the next

rules.do: Set `multiple` when people compare items side by side
rules.dont: Leave items that are read together closing each other

rules.do: Set the heading level with `slotProps.header.render` (`render: <h4 />`) when the accordion sits under an `h3`; under a panel's or a dialog's `h2`, keep the `h3`
rules.dont: Leave the outline skipping a level, or wrap the title in a heading of your own inside the button

rules.do: Use `hiddenUntilFound` on long help pages, so the browser's find in page reaches closed answers
rules.dont: Use `keepMounted` to make closed content searchable: a `hidden` panel is out of find in page as well

rules.do: Leave out an item whose panel would have nothing in it, or open it to an [EmptyState](empty-state.md) that says why
rules.dont: Disable an item because its panel has nothing to show: a disabled trigger can't say why, and it leaves the Tab order

props.name: children

props.name: action

props.name: slotProps
